shots.focal_element: A washed-out 'Brand kits' list page (Headphone Corp and Tropical Hotel Group cards) with the form editor ghosted faintly behind it
shots.typography: Native product UI only: regular-weight sans page heading 'Brand kits' in sentence case, small white-on-black button label with a plus glyph, regular sans card titles and truncated footer labels; default tracking. No added motion-graphics type.
shots.what_happens: Outro bridge: the Brand kits list sits under a strong white wash, double-exposed over the faded editor, while the cursor idles at the top right and the VO says 'Stay on brand with' (w270-w273). The image is otherwise static; in the final sampled frame (2:17.5) it has dissolved to white with a grey 'Typeform' wordmark fading in.
shots.build_rebuild: Crossfade a Brand kits screenshot in under an ~85% white overlay on top of the fading editor capture, hold it static for ~2.5 s, then dissolve the whole frame to a white background over ~0.4 s while the centred wordmark fades from 0 to full opacity.

shots.focal_element: Centred black 'Typeform' wordmark on a plain white background
shots.typography: Single wordmark in a geometric/humanist sans, bold-ish (semi-bold) weight, title case, normal tracking (low-confidence guess: Typeform's own brand sans)
shots.what_happens: End card: the Typeform wordmark holds centred on white, fully static, for ~3.4 s as the VO finishes 'Typeform.' (w274) and the music plays out to the end of the video.
shots.build_rebuild: Render a white full-frame background with a centred black wordmark at ~22% of frame width and hold it static for ~3.4 s until the end of the video.

hook.text: Put your brand front and center with Typeforms Brand Kit. (VO over a title card reading 'Add brand assets to your typeforms with Brand Kit')

cta.text: Stay on brand with Typeform. (spoken sign-off over the wordmark; no on-screen action, URL or button)

summary.tone: Friendly, calm and instructional: a help-centre style walkthrough with a warm conversational narrator, light background music and a short designed intro before real-time product screen recording.

signature_moments.description: A pink colour swatch slides across the plain form's headline and, inside its mask, the text re-renders in the themed serif style, a 'theme lens' that visualises what setting a colour palette does.
signature_moments.why_premium: It explains the feature's value in under a second without words, using a masked dual-layer reveal that reads as bespoke motion design rather than a screen capture.

signature_moments.description: The intro builds a recreated form that gains a logo, then fans into a diagonal cascade of three themed versions (yellow, pink, teal); the demo later produces those same three Tropical themes for real.
signature_moments.why_premium: The intro previews the exact end state of the tutorial, so the screen recording pays off a promise already made visually, giving the piece a planned narrative arc.

signature_moments.description: Spotlight holds dim the whole editor except the Brand Kit palette popover and the theme card stack, landing on the narration ('color palettes', 'here').
signature_moments.why_premium: Directed attention on dense UI turns a raw recording into a guided read, a small post-production touch that many tutorials skip.

hook.evidence: A clear benefit line spoken over a clean squircle title card, followed by a slide-out exit, but the card is static for ~2.7 s and makes no stat, question or pain point; competent rather than gripping.

clarity.evidence: Every VO line maps to a visible click (Brand kit sidebar, Create brand kit, Colors '+', Themes tab, Design tab, theme card), push-ins and spotlights point to the active control, and the payoff is shown explicitly. The 37 s single shot s012 packs many steps and an in-shot jump edit, which slows the read.

ui_showcase.evidence: Real product UI at legible scale with digital push-ins (s008, s010, s014, s023), spotlight dims (s015, s021) and a before/after theme swap on the canvas; plus a stylised recreated form in the intro. Much of the middle is unzoomed full-frame recording.

motion_polish.evidence: The intro (panel slide, wipe-up, swatch mask, themed card cascade) is crafted, but the body relies on crossfades, simple digital zooms and real-time cursor moves, with a visible jump edit in s012 and a washed-out double-exposure outro bridge in s024.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchors audio facts plus visuals: music bed at 136 BPM throughout at -18.26 LUFS integrated; designed whoosh/swoosh/impact SFX (x001-x003) only in the intro transitions; the rest of the 21 SFX candidates are mostly diegetic typing/click sounds from the recording (x007-x020) plus one chime (x021, ~99.2 s) near the theme being applied in s016. Clean and unobtrusive but not sculpted to the edit.

vo_script_quality.evidence: 275 words in ~141 s, plain imperative steps ('click here in the bottom-left corner', 'Under the Design tab') with sequencing markers (First, Then, Finally) and a clear payoff line 'instantly branded Typeform'. Slightly long-winded side branches (delete assets w123-w145, editing from the form w249-w269).

brand_consistency.evidence: Bookended by a Typeform title card and wordmark end card in the same sans; the demo brand (THG pink/teal/yellow themes, serif type) introduced in the recreated intro carries consistently through every demo stage to the final branded form.

works_muted.evidence: No captions or overlay labels; with sound off the cursor clicks, push-ins and spotlights still show the path (sidebar, create kit, add assets, theme, apply), and the before/after theme swap is visible, but the reasons and some steps (e.g. long s012) rely on the VO.

overall.evidence: A competent, clear product tutorial with a well-designed 13 s animated intro and good attention-direction touches, but most of its 141 s is real-time screen recording with basic transitions and a plain outro, so it reads as polished help content rather than a premium launch explainer.

localization_friendliness.notes: The title card text is baked into the intro and nearly every frame is an English product UI screen recording (sidebar, buttons, file names, typed names), so localising means re-recording the UI in each language; the steps also lean on the VO. Only the end card (wordmark) and the wordless intro animation (s002-s005) transfer as-is.
